related_questions.question: What is the best antiviral drug for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Paxlovid, an oral antiviral pill that can be taken at home, is the go-to treatment for COVID-19. If you are at high risk for severe disease from COVID, and you take it within the first five days of experiencing symptoms, it will lower your risk of getting so sick that you need to be hospitalized.

text_blocks.snippet: Ivermectin is primarily used to treat parasitic infections, not viral infections. While some in-vitro studies have shown potential antiviral effects against viruses like Zika and SARS-CoV-2, these findings require further research and clinical validation. The FDA has not authorized ivermectin for treating or preventing COVID-19.

list.title: Primary Use:
list.snippet: Ivermectin is an anti-parasitic drug used to treat various parasitic infections in both humans and animals.

list.title: Antiviral Potential:
list.snippet: Research has explored ivermectin's potential antiviral properties against several viruses, including:
Zika Virus: Some studies have indicated potential antiviral activity in laboratory settings, but these findings have not translated to successful treatment in animal models.

SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19): A 2020 study showed that ivermectin reduced SARS-CoV-2 replication in cells, according to a study published by the National Institutes of Health (NIH). However, this study was conducted in vitro (in a lab setting) and has not been validated by subsequent clinical trials.

list.title: FDA Position:
list.snippet: The FDA has not approved or authorized ivermectin for treating or preventing COVID-19. The agency advises against using ivermectin for COVID-19 outside of a clinical trial or a prescription from a healthcare provider.

related_questions.question: What is the best thing to take for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: The "best" treatment for COVID-19 depends on individual risk factors and the severity of symptoms. For those at high risk for severe illness, antiviral medications like Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir) or Lagevrio (molnupiravir) can be effective, especially when started early in the infection. However, these medications are not recommended for everyone and may have side effects or interactions with other medications. It's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional to determine the most appropriate course of action, according to the CDC.
snippet_highlighted_words: antiviral medications like Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir) or Lagevrio (molnupiravir)

text_blocks.snippet: General recommendations for managing COVID-19 include:

list.title: Isolation:
list.snippet: Continue to isolate while taking antiviral medication, says the Wisconsin Department of Health Services.

list.title: Symptom management:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help with fever and pain. Rest and hydration are also important.

list.title: Monitoring:
list.snippet: Watch for worsening symptoms and seek medical attention if needed, advises the CDC.

list.title: Consult with a healthcare professional:
list.snippet: They can assess individual risk factors, determine if antiviral medication is appropriate, and provide personalized advice.
